chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a judge who arbitrates between two parties and takes sustenance from the ruler for judging, so he said, 'That is the spoils of war (suh't).'

key_terms.السُّحْتُ: Spoils of war / specific type of wealth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a judge's salary from the ruler in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) characterizes the salary of a judge appointed by the ruler as 'al-suh't'. While 'suh't' literally refers to spoils of war, Shia jurists often interpret it here as a specific type of wealth acquired through authority or power, distinguishing it from standard wages and implying a distinct legal status for judicial remuneration under the caliphs. This highlights the nuanced Shia view on the legitimacy of judicial appointments and their compensation during periods of political transition.
